by_judge.judge: CHIEF JUSTICE & K.S. HEMALEKHA & VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL
K V ARAVIND WILL SIT IN COURT HALL NO.4 AT KALABURAGI
D K SINGH & VENKATESH NAIK T

narrative:
On August 7, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 39.6%, adjudicating 936 out of 2,363 scheduled matters across 63 judges. This performance reflects a slight increase from the previous week's conversion rate of 38.1% (879 of 2,307) on July 31, 2026, though it remains below earlier benchmarks set on July 17 (49.2%) and June 5 (41.4%).

Judicial clearance rates varied widely across court halls. The division bench of Chief Justice & K.S. Hemalekha achieved a 100% hearing rate on their main list, taking up all 25 scheduled matters. Among single-judge benches handling heavy workloads, R. Nataraj disposed of 54 out of 83 cases (65.1%) and Suraj Govindaraj converted 57 of 92 matters (62.0%) in Court Hall 10. Conversely, benches facing massive dockets saw lower completion percentages: S Vishwajith Shetty was assigned 210 cases—the day's largest individual roster—hearing 64 (30.5%), while B M Shyam Prasad converted 7 of 116 scheduled matters (6.0%) on a primary list segment.

By stage of proceeding, interlocutory and preliminary stages moved faster than substantive hearings. Both Orders (321 of 734) and Preliminary Hearings (138 of 316) reached a 43.7% hearing rate, while Admissions saw 35.7% (159 of 446) heard. In contrast, Final Hearings lagged behind, converting only 23.5% of scheduled cases (92 of 392).

Subject matter distribution was dominated by Writ Petitions (WP), which comprised 1,061 scheduled cases and achieved a 38.3% hearing rate (406 heard). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) followed with 362 cases scheduled and 167 heard (46.1%). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) recorded a 34.4% rate (95 of 276), whereas smaller procedural categories achieved much higher clearance, notably Criminal Revision Petitions (CRL.RP) at 81.5% (22 of 27) and Review Petitions (RP) at 69.4% (25 of 36).
